properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST Sunday.

* At 352 PM MST, a river gauge on the Paria River reported a rapid
rise from heavy rain over the Paria River drainage basin. Flood
waters will proceed down the Paria River drainage this evening
reaching Lees Ferry between about 8 to 10 PM MST.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry and Vermilion Cliffs National Monument.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry around 8:00 to 10:00 PM MST.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 830 PM MST.

* At 341 PM MST, the river guage on Oak Creek near Sedona remained
near flood stage, with futher rises expected. Oak Creek at
Cornville remained above moderate flood stage. emergency management
has reported flooding around Tlaquepaque in Sedona. Flash flooding
is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 3:00pm the stage was 16.94 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A is expected at late this evening around 19 feet.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Inundation begins to affect fish hatchery across from
gauge site.
At 21.0 feet: Stream reaches bridge at Page Springs Rd.
...
For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 2:45pm the stage was 13.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest is expected late this evening near 18 feet.
Impacts:
At 13.0 feet: Stream reaches terrace under Tlaquepaque bridge. Low
water crossings closed.
At 14.0 feet: Flood stage. Several islands downstream in Sedona
evacuated. Minor flooding of access roads, buildings, and
residences along Oak Creek.
At 16.0 feet: Flooding begins at Rancho Sedona RV Park on Bear
Wallow Lane, Trails End Drive, Oak Creek Mobilodge, Poco Diablo
Resort on Sycamore Road and Oak Creek Cliffs Drive, and Chavez
Crossing Campground.
At 18.0 feet: Minor damage to shops and galleries near the
Tlaquepaque bridge.
At 20.0 feet: Major flooding to mobile homes downstream from the
Tlaquepaque bridge and access roads along Oak Creek through Sedona.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Bignotti, Indian Gardens,
Pine Flats, Uptown Sedona, Sedona Airport, Red Rock State Park,
